title: Regional Load-Shedding Sentinel with Decaying Trip-Score and Variant Throttle
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a regional load-shedding sentinel that automatically triggers graceful fallbacks and throttles variant traffic when overload signals appear (429 spikes, timeouts, elevated error-rate, rising latency p95). The sentinel should be region-aware and tier-aware: it reduces or redirects traffic per-customer tier and per-region, and progressively shifts requests to cheaper or more robust model variants rather than a hard failover. Key goals: avoid global outages, preserve high-priority customer SLAs, and minimize cost/regression from fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Trip-score computed for each region+route with configurable weights for 429s, timeouts, error-rate, and latency percentiles.
Trip-score decays exponentially when signals improve (configurable half-life) to prevent oscillation.
On trip threshold breach, routing policy reduces routed weight to primary variant by a configurable step and moves traffic to fallback variants over N windows rather than immediate cutover.
Circuit breaker exposes states: CLOSED -> PROBING -> OPEN -> HALF_OPEN with observable transitions and per-tenant overrides.
Per-variant throttle quotas applied (concurrency and qps) with soft-fallback to next variant if a variant is overloaded.
Integration test coverage for simulated 429/timeouts and load tests validating no >5% higher error-rate for P0 customers during staged rollouts.
Runtime metrics emit: trip_score, trip_state, variant_weights, per-region-routing_rate, fallback_shift_events with tags (region, tier, route, model_variant).
Feature flag gate present; rollout can be toggled per-region and per-team in console.
proposed_solution: Compute a rolling trip_score per region-route combining: exponentially weighted moving average of 429 ratio, timeout ratio, error-rate, and a normalized latency p95 metric. Use configurable coefficients per signal.
Apply an exponential decay to historic signals with a tunable half_life (default 2m) to avoid brittle flip-flops.

Define configurable trip thresholds: warning, trip, and hard-trip. Warning emits alerts but does not change routing. Trip moves to PROBING and reduces primary variant weight by step_percent (default 20%) every evaluation window until stable fallback weight reached or hard-trip triggers full divert.
Introduce per-variant throttle controller which enforces concurrency/QPS caps and communicates back pressure to the sentinel so throttled variants are deprioritized in the next evaluation window.
Circuit breaker state machine implemented in routing layer with protobuf-defined state events; persist state with TTL in central state store (Redis cluster with regional replication).

Routing decisions should prefer model variants that are resource-similar to the primary (e.g., same architecture quantized variant) before routing to cheaper/shorter-context variants, to preserve output quality.
Expose APIs for manual override and per-customer policy pins (can pin to primary or allow automatic fallback).
design_decisions: Use a score-based approach instead of simple counters to combine multiple signals and provide a single control surface for thresholding.
Exponential decay selected over sliding-window hysteresis because it reduces memory and simplifies cross-region comparisons.
Staged weight-shifting chosen (gradual stepping) to avoid sharp quality cliffs when switching variants.
Persisting state in Redis chosen for low-latency reads/writes and existing operational familiarity; add raft-backed fallback for leader election in failure scenarios.
Avoid model-quality automatic regression detection in initial rollout to limit blast radius; separate eval pipeline will monitor quality regressions tied to rollout events.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal canary): enable sentinel in two non-production regions with feature flag; run synthetic 429/timeouts injections and verify trip_score behavior.
Phase 2 (limited customers): open to 5% of production traffic in low-risk regions; monitor P95 latency, 429 spike counts, and customer impact dashboards for 48h.
Phase 3 (regional expansion): enable in selected regions with gradual ramp to 50% traffic by automating step_percent reductions; keep global guardrail to avoid >30% traffic shift per hour.
Phase 4 (full): enable standard policy for all regions and add per-customer overrides in console.
Rollback: feature flag off or set hard-trip to noop; immediate fallback to CLOSED restores weights; alerting runbook prepared for manual intervention.
monitoring_and_alerting: Critical alerts: trip_score > hard_trip_threshold for >2 consecutive windows for regions with >1% traffic -> page on-call SRE.
Warning alerts: rapid increase in trip_score (>50% change) -> slack channel #routing-alerts and automated runbook link.
Dashboards: per-region timeline showing trip_score, variant weight shifts, and customer error-rate overlays with an annotation for rollout events.
SLO guardrails: if any P0 customer experiences >2x baseline error-rate after a fallback event, auto-open incident and rollback policy.
testing_plan: Unit tests for trip_score calculation with synthetic time-series inputs and configurable coefficients.
Integration tests exercising state transitions of circuit breaker (CLOSED -> PROBING -> OPEN -> HALF_OPEN -> CLOSED) with mocked throttles.
Chaos test: inject 429 storms and timeouts in regional instances during canary to validate gradual weight shift and no global failover.
Load test: run production-scale load in staging with tiered customer traffic shapes to validate per-tier policies and guardrails.
Quality-check: run existing eval suites against a representative prompt set during staged variant shifts to detect regressions.
open_questions: What default coefficients should we use for combining 429s vs timeouts vs latency? (proposal: 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1 for 429, timeout, error-rate, p95 respectively).
Should hard-trip immediately divert all traffic for P0 customers if severe region-wide outage is detected, or always preserve manual override?
Operational cost: what is acceptable extra cost from routing to multiple variants during long-running partial fallbacks? Need finance input.
How should we tie fallback events to the Optimize recommendations to suggest permanent model changes (e.g., quantize primary)?
